key_insight: An LLM extracted comorbidities and their dates from clinical text with high agreement for diagnosis presence and earliest reported dates, but lower agreement for complete date sets.
clinical_relevance: Automated temporal extraction could support longitudinal registry development while reducing direct annotation costs.
method: Applied gpt-oss-20b to 2,343 clinical entries from 248 Bern Sleep-Wake Registry patients.
Extracted diagnosis presence, instance counts, and dates across 32 diagnostic categories in six comorbidity groups.
Compared outputs with an adjudicated physician reference standard and assessed direct annotation costs.
evidence_signal: Diagnosis-presence F1 was 0.88, earliest-date day-level agreement was 86.73%, and direct annotation costs were reduced by 94.65%.
watch_item: Complete date-set agreement was only 58.19%, with a 20.88% extra-date rate; temporal outputs need careful validation before downstream use.
paper_title: Bern Sleep-Wake Registry: temporal extraction of comorbidities from unstructured clinical text using a large language model
